name: Refugio antiaéreo de Villanueva de Córdoba
story: Villanueva de Córdoba lay in the Republican-held north of Córdoba province, close to the front around Pozoblanco. In March–April 1937 Queipo de Llano's forces tried to break through to the Almadén mercury mines and were stopped at Pozoblanco by Republican forces under Joaquín Pérez Salas and others; the front then stayed close by until the end of the war. Nationalist aircraft bombed the towns of the area, and in 1937 Villanueva built an underground shelter beneath its main square. It is one of the declared Places of Democratic Memory in Andalusia.
see: An underground shelter beneath the Plaza de España.
plan: Visits by arrangement; ask at the town hall or tourist office in the Plaza de España.
